results.question: which category brings in the most revenue?
results.interpretation: Which menu category (Whole Pie, Slice, Wings, Drink, Side) has generated the most revenue across all non-cancelled orders?
results.sql: SELECT mi.category, SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY mi.category ORDER BY revenue DESC

results.question: which item sells the most?
results.interpretation: Which menu item has the highest total quantity sold across all non-cancelled orders?
results.sql: SELECT mi.name, mi.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY mi.id, mi.name, mi.category ORDER BY total_sold DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: who are our top 5 customers by how much they've spent?
results.interpretation: The 5 customers who have spent the most in total across all their non-cancelled orders, with their total spend.
results.sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price) AS total_spent, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.city ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5

results.question: how many drinks do we have in stock?
results.interpretation: Show how many of each drink are currently in stock, from current inventory rather than the nightly restock target.
results.sql: SELECT mi.name, i.quantity AS in_stock FROM inventory i JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = i.menu_item_id WHERE mi.category = 'Drink' ORDER BY mi.name;

results.question: what's in the most recent order?
results.interpretation: Show the line items (item name, quantity, price, line total) in the most recently placed order.
results.sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT o.id, o.created_at, o.status, o.customer_id FROM orders o ORDER BY o.created_at DESC, o.id DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT l.id AS order_id, l.created_at, l.status, c.name AS customer_name, mi.name AS item, oi.quantity, mi.price, oi.quantity * mi.price AS line_total FROM latest l JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = l.id JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id = l.customer_id ORDER BY oi.id

results.question: show me the latest 3 orders with what was in each
results.interpretation: Show the 3 most recently placed orders (by time placed), one row per order, with the customer, status, the items in each order, item count, and order total.
results.sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer, o.status, o.created_at, STRING_AGG(oi.quantity || 'x ' || mi.name, ', ' ORDER BY mi.name) AS items, SUM(oi.quantity) AS item_count, SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price) AS total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id GROUP BY o.id, c.name, o.status, o.created_at ORDER BY o.created_at DESC, o.id DESC LIMIT 3

results.question: what share of our revenue comes from slices?
results.interpretation: What percentage of total revenue (all non-cancelled orders) comes from items in the 'Slice' category.
results.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN mi.category = 'Slice' THEN oi.quantity * mi.price ELSE 0 END) AS slice_revenue, SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price) AS total_revenue, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN mi.category = 'Slice' THEN oi.quantity * mi.price ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price), 0), 2) AS slice_share_pct FROM order_items oi JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled'

results.question: which day of the week gets the most orders?
results.interpretation: Count orders (excluding cancelled ones) by day of the week, based on when each order was placed in New York time, and show the busiest day first.
results.sql: SELECT to_char(created_at, 'FMDay') AS day_of_week, EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM created_at) AS day_num, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY to_char(created_at, 'FMDay'), EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM created_at) ORDER BY order_count DESC, day_num

results.question: how many customers have never ordered wings?
results.interpretation: Count of customers who have never had a Wings item in any of their orders (excluding cancelled orders as purchases).
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_never_ordered_wings FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND mi.category = 'Wings' AND o.status <> 'Cancelled');

results.question: what was our total revenue in June 2026?
results.interpretation: Total revenue (quantity × price across all non-cancelled orders) for orders dated in June 2026.
results.sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price), 0) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' AND o.order_date >= DATE '2026-06-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-07-01';

results.question: on average, how many items are in an order?
results.interpretation: The average number of items (total quantity across all line items) per order, counting all orders except cancelled ones.
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(item_count), 2) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT o.id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS item_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY o.id) t;

results.question: which Brooklyn customer has spent the most?
results.interpretation: Find the customer located in Brooklyn with the highest total spend across all non-cancelled orders.
results.sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id WHERE c.city ILIKE '%brooklyn%' AND o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.city ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: how many orders were placed in the last hour?
results.interpretation: Count of orders placed within the past 60 minutes (based on each order's created_at timestamp), including all statuses.
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_last_hour FROM orders WHERE created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '1 hour';

results.question: how many customers have ordered more than once?
results.interpretation: Count of customers who have placed more than one order (excluding cancelled orders).
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers FROM (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) t;

results.question: what's our cancellation rate?
results.interpretation: The share of all orders that have status 'Cancelled', shown as cancelled count, total orders, and percentage.
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Cancelled') AS cancelled_orders, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Cancelled') / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS cancellation_rate_pct FROM orders

results.question: which menu items have never been ordered?
results.interpretation: List the menu items that don't appear on any order (excluding cancelled orders isn't applied — any order at all counts as having been ordered).
results.sql: SELECT mi.id, mi.name, mi.category, mi.price FROM menu_items mi WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.menu_item_id = mi.id) ORDER BY mi.category, mi.name;

results.question: what's the busiest hour of the day for orders?
results.interpretation: Which hour of the day (New York time) has the most orders placed, across all order history, excluding cancelled orders.
results.sql: SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM o.created_at)::int AS hour_of_day, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY order_count DESC, hour_of_day LIMIT 1;

results.question: how much revenue did we make in the last 7 days?
results.interpretation: Total revenue (quantity × price) from all non-cancelled orders placed in the last 7 days.
results.sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * mi.price), 0) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN menu_items mi ON mi.id = oi.menu_item_id JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'Cancelled' AND o.created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '7 days';

results.question: how long ago was the most recent order placed?
results.interpretation: How much time has passed since the most recent order was placed (based on its created_at timestamp).
results.sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer, o.created_at, now() - o.created_at AS time_ago FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.created_at DESC, o.id DESC LIMIT 1
